land.text: the Denkyira kingdom, 'reduced to a tributary of the newly ascendant Asante Empire' after Feyiase (August 1701)

successors.note: The Ashanti dossier (af-04-a) founds the Ashanti in 1701 with counterpart denkyira. The Denkyirahene stayed on as a tributary: rebellions 1706-1707 and 1823/24, alignment with the Fante Confederacy in 1868, infobox '1896 (as independent kingdom)'.

capitals.name: Abankeseso (Ntibanso)
capitals.note: Capital Abankeseso; the page gives no coordinates, so the dot is placed at Dunkwa-on-Offin, the Upper Denkyira town the Boa Amponsem page links to Boamponsem (approximate).

correction.text: the Denkyira kingdom, 'the dominant Akan power in the Ofin-Pra basin' by the mid-17th century, capital Abankeseso

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no founding year, no area and no frontier (the infobox has a map 'Denkyira at its greatest extent, c. 1699'); a 70 km circle round Obuasi (about 21,000 km2 of land cells) stands for the Ofin-Pra basin.

correction.text: Denkyira at its greatest extent: 'In 1698, Denkyira conquered Assin'; 'By the end of the decade, it reached the western region of the Tano basin'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1650 core plus a 35 km circle round Assin Fosu for Assin. The Tano-basin reach is not drawn (no town named). Infobox map caption 'greatest extent, c. 1699'; no area figure.

ledger.note: 1650s: Boamponsem makes Denkyira the great power of the Ofin-Pra basin. He was Denkyirahene 'from the 1650s until his death in 1694'; 'By the mid-17th century, the kingdom had become the dominant Akan power in the Ofin-Pra basin' (Denkyira page). No founding year on any page; 1650 is the start of the 1650s.
1698: Denkyira conquers Assin. 'In 1698, Denkyira conquered Assin, destroying its towns and markets and imposing heavy tribute.'

region.text: Kwaaman, the Asante core round Kumasi, and Feyiase

ledger.note: 1701: Denkyira marches north against Kwaaman. 'In 1701, Denkyira launched a northern campaign against Kwaaman'; Denkyiran gains at Adunku, Abuontem and Aputuogya preceded the battle (Feyiase page).

region.text: Feyiase Akoyem, now in Bosomtwe District

ledger.note: 1701 (August): Feyiase decides the war. 'At the decisive Battle of Feyiase, Denkyira's forces were routed and Denkyirahene Ntim Gyakari was killed' (Denkyira page); the Feyiase infobox gives 'August, 1701' and 'Asante victory; Fall of Denkyira kingdom'.

1701 (August): Denkyira passes to Asante. 'Following this defeat, Denkyira was reduced to a tributary of the newly ascendant Asante Empire.' The Feyiase page names no terms, no tribute and no annexation.

1701 (August): the Denkyira kingdom falls. 'In 1701, Denkyira was defeated by the Asante Empire and became a vassal.' It rebelled between 1706 and 1707 ('the uprising was crushed') and in 1823 ('but were defeated'; 1824 in the lead).

wars.name: Denkyira-Agona conflict with Akwamu
wars.outcome: 'In 1688 it supported Agona in a conflict with Akwamu, and later attempted to invade Fetu'; no outcome and no land on the page (Akwamu's last major campaign against Agona was in 1689).

wars.name: Denkyira conquest of Assin
wars.outcome: Denkyira conquered Assin, destroying its towns and markets and imposing heavy tribute.

wars.name: Battle of Feyiase
wars.outcome: Asante victory in August 1701: Ntim Gyakari killed, Denkyira's hegemony broken and the kingdom reduced to a tributary of Asante; Denkyira's army had two or three Dutch cannons, taken by the Asante.
wars.note: Denkyira had gained at Adunku, Abuontem and Aputuogya before the ambush; the war ended between Aputuogya and Esereso.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shape is a circle and a town standing for the Ofin-Pra basin and Assin.

sources.title: Denkyira
sources.note: Lead (1701 vassal, 1824/1823 rebellion), Ofin-Pra basin, 1698 Assin, 1688 Agona, 1692 envoys, 1694 Boamponsem, 1701 campaign and Feyiase, 1706-07 rebellion, infobox 1896; no founding year, no area.

sources.title: Battle of Feyiase
sources.note: August 1701; Ntim Gyakari killed; result "Asante victory; Fall of Denkyira kingdom"; no post-battle terms.

sources.title: Boa Amponsem I
sources.note: Denkyirahene "from the 1650s until his death in 1694"; no conquests, no vassals, no extent.

notes: Denkyira has no Cliopatria row. Three pages opened (the main page twice for different sections). The pages give no founding year, no area and no frontier, so the 1650 start and every shape are low-confidence readings (the 1650 start is the 'from the 1650s' of the Boa Amponsem page). The Ashanti dossier (af-04-a) takes Denkyira as its predecessor at 1701; here the Denkyira land is a `loss` to ashanti-empire, with the tributary Denkyirahene continuing to 1896 in the infobox but not as a state with a dossier. Disagreements: Denkyira page lead 1824 vs later section 1823 for the rebellion; Boamponsem 'from the 1650s' with no year; the Denkyira page says the Dutch, English and Brandenburgers reached Abankeseso in 1692, the Boa Amponsem page says he sent an envoy to the Gold Coast and does not mention Brandenburgers. Not placed: the Tano basin (no town named), Twifo-Heman, Akyem, Fetu (conquest dates not on the page), and Adansi (infobox 'Conquest of Adansi' undated). Gazetteer names needed: Assin Fosu (Central Region, Ghana, about 5.7N 1.28W). Counterparts without dossier: Assin, Agona, Adansi, Kwaaman.
